tolerance.basis: linear (inviscid, potential) sloshing dispersion; the tolerance covers the thin-tank/3-D correction which is O(1e-3) for L/B ~ 2

source.doc: Faltinsen, O.M. & Timokha, A.N., 'Sloshing', Cambridge University Press (2009), ch. 4 (linear 2-D tank modes); primary equations also in Abramson, H.N. (ed.), 'The Dynamic Behavior of Liquids in Moving Containers', NASA SP-106 (1966)
source.table: rectangular tank natural frequency, mode n=1: omega^2 = g (n pi / L) tanh(n pi h / L)
source.access_note: closed form transcribed from the textbook/NASA report equations; page numbers not re-verified offline

sha256_scope: sha256 over the archived digitisation artefact (sources/faltinsen2000.rect_sloshing_omega1.csv), i.e. the byte-exact table this entry serves; no page image of the source document is held in-repo, so the anchor does not claim pixel-level provenance

validity_range.note: 2-D (L/B -> infinity) linear theory; finite tank width and nonlinearity are outside this entry's validity

dual_pass.note: pass A = machine-precision transcription of the published closed form; pass B = re-typed at printed precision (5-6 s.f.) with an independent format convention. Human double-keying is NOT claimed.

verification.method: analytic limits of the same dispersion relation: deep-water limit at h/L=2 vs sqrt(k) gives the deviation caused by tanh(kh); shallow-water check at h/L=0.1

notes: Mode n=1; tabulated as omega*sqrt(L/g) so that it serves any tank length.
Non-monotone-free? omega is monotone increasing in h/L, so the PCHIP/linear consistency criterion is evaluated on a single monotone segment.
